Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 1) Subtopic: Certificates, Death Certificate, Referral/Discharge, ICD-10 & Forensic Psychiatry 1. Medical certificates are classified as:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Medical certificates are written documents and are therefore documentary evidence. Fitness, illness, birth and death certificates are examples.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 2) Fitness certificate is a type of:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Fitness certificate is a medical certificate. It documents a person’s medical fitness for a specific purpose.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 3) Age certificate is usually issued after:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Age certificate is issued after clinical and radiological assessment. It is often used for legal or school purposes.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 4) Injury report is mainly used in:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Injury report is a medico-legal report used in assault, accident and violence cases. It includes physical findings and opinion on weapon or nature of injury.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 5) Postmortem report usually gives opinion about:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Postmortem report records autopsy findings. It usually gives opinion regarding cause and approximate time of death.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 6) Sexual assault report includes:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Sexual assault report includes general examination, genital examination and collection of forensic evidence. It has important medico-legal value.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 7) Toxicology report is mainly used in:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Toxicology report is used in suspected poisoning. It includes clinical examination and laboratory findings.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 8) Name, age, sex, address and occupation in a medico-legal report are:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Demographic information identifies the examined person. It includes name, age, sex, address and occupation.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 9) Signature, seal, date and designation of doctor represent:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Authentication validates a medico-legal document. Signature, seal, date and designation show responsibility and official status.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 10) Proper handling and transfer of samples/documents is called:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Chain of custody ensures proper handling and transfer of evidence. It maintains legal reliability of samples and documents.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 11) Death certificate may be issued when death is due to:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Death certificate may be issued when death is natural, cause is known, and the doctor attended the patient during last illness.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 12) For issuing death certificate, the cause of death should be:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: A doctor should issue death certificate only when the cause of death is known. Unknown or suspicious cases need medico-legal handling.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 13) The doctor issuing death certificate should have attended the patient during:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: The doctor should have attended the patient during the last illness. This makes the opinion on cause of death reliable.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 14) Before issuing death certificate, the doctor should be satisfied about:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: The doctor must be satisfied about the identity of the deceased and the cause of death. Wrong certification may create legal problems.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 15) In suspicious death, the doctor should:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Suspicious death is a medico-legal case. Ordinary death certificate should not be issued as natural death.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 16) In suspected poisoning, death certificate should be:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.option2: Withheld as ordinary natural death certificate
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Poisoning is an unnatural medico-legal death. Ordinary natural death certificate should not be issued.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 17) The tripod of life consists of brain, heart and:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: The tripod of life includes brain, heart and lungs. Failure of these vital systems produces the modes of death.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 18) Mode of death due to brain failure is:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Coma is the mode of death due to failure of brain function. Syncope is heart failure and asphyxia is respiratory failure.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 19) Mode of death due to heart failure is:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Syncope is the mode of death due to failure of heart function. It represents circulatory failure.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 20) Mode of death due to respiratory failure is:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Asphyxia is the mode of death due to respiratory failure. It results from failure of oxygenation.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 21) Immediate postmortem change includes stoppage of:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Immediate changes after death are stoppage of brain function, respiration and circulation. These reflect failure of the tripod of life.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 22) Early postmortem changes include:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.option1: Pallor, cooling, lividity and rigor mortis
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Early postmortem changes include pallor, cooling, lividity and rigor mortis. Late changes include putrefaction, adipocere and mummification.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 23) Late postmortem changes include:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Putrefaction, adipocere and mummification are late postmortem changes. These occur after early changes have appeared.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 24) The surest sign of death is:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Putrefaction is the surest sign of death. It indicates definite decomposition of the body.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 25) Death certificate should be prepared properly and authentically as per:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Death certificate should be prepared as per ICD-10. ICD-10 standardizes cause-of-death recording.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 26) Death trance is also called:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Death trance or suspended animation is a state where vital signs are extremely faint. The person may appear dead but life persists.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 27) Referral certificate mainly documents:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Referral certificate documents transfer of a patient to another doctor or facility. It should include clinical condition and reason for referral.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 28) Discharge certificate is issued when:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Discharge certificate summarizes hospital treatment, condition at discharge and advice. It supports continuity of care.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 29) Condition at discharge is mainly recorded in:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Discharge certificate should include condition at discharge. It also records diagnosis, treatment given and follow-up advice.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 30) The reason for referral is mainly recorded in:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Referral certificate should clearly mention the reason for referral. This helps the next doctor continue care appropriately.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 31) Forensic medicine means:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.option1: Medical knowledge used for legal investigation
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.option3: Legal rules applied to hospital billing
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Forensic medicine applies medical knowledge to legal investigation. It deals with crime, injury, death, poisoning, rape and identification.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 32) Medical jurisprudence means:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.option4: Legal rules applied to medical practice
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Medical jurisprudence deals with law guiding medical practice. It includes consent, negligence, ethics, confidentiality and professional misconduct.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 33) Forensic psychiatry is:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Forensic psychiatry applies psychiatric knowledge to legal issues. It includes assessment of mental state and legal responsibility.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 34) McNaughten Rule is a test for:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: McNaughten Rule is a legal test for insanity. It assesses criminal responsibility in relation to unsoundness of mind.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 35) Under McNaughten Rule, a person may not be criminally responsible if due to unsoundness of mind he did not know:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.option3: Nature of the act or that the act was wrong
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: McNaughten Rule says the person is not criminally responsible if he did not know the nature of the act or that it was wrong or illegal.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 36) Durham Rule is associated with:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Durham Rule is listed as a USA legal test related to mental state. McNaughten Rule remains the key legal insanity rule in the file.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 37) Forensic pathology deals mainly with:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Forensic pathology deals with cause and manner of death. It is closely related to autopsy and death investigation.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 38) Forensic thanatology deals with:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.option2: Medical and legal aspects of death
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Forensic thanatology deals with death and autopsy-related medico-legal issues. It includes medical and legal aspects of death.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 39) Forensic radiology is mainly related to:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Forensic radiology uses X-ray examination for legal purposes. It is useful in age and sex determination.

Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.question: 40) Forensic serology deals with:
Forensic psychiatry & Certificates.exp: Forensic serology deals with blood and seminal stains. It is important in assault and sexual offence cases.
